en: to go through hardships; to have difficulty

examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 젊을 때 고생고생하며 사셨어요.
examples.en: My parents lived through many hardships when they were young.
I had a really hard time all week because of moving.

examples.ko: 그 길을 찾느라 고생고생해서 겨우 도착했어요.
examples.en: I struggled so much to find the way that I barely arrived.
I am thankful to my mother, who went through so much raising children.
I have so much luggage that I am struggling on the stairs.
After going through so much hardship, I finally passed.

explain: '고생하다'를 반복해서 힘든 일을 오래, 많이 겪었다는 느낌을 더해요. 하소연하거나 지난 일을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요. 윗사람에게는 '고생고생하시다'처럼 높여요.

phrases.en: After going through so much hardship, I finally bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 노력한 끝에 결과를 얻었다는 말을 이어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the hardship to the result achieved afterward.

phrases.en: Grandmother went through so much hardship raising us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람의 힘든 일을 높여서 말하는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for an older person's hardships.

phrases.en: I had a really hard time moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고생고생하다'보다 덜 하소연하는 느낌이라 일상에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less of a complaint than 고생고생하다; easy to use in daily talk.

explain_en: It repeats '고생하다' to add the feeling of having gone through hard things for a long time. It fits venting or telling stories about the past. For elders, make it honorific like '고생고생하시다'.

examples.en: The child bobs his head to the song.

examples.ko: 그녀는 알겠다는 듯 고개를 까닥거리며 웃었어요.
examples.en: She smiled, nodding slightly as if she understood.
Why do you keep bobbing your toes?
Grandfather just nodded slightly without a word.
He beckoned me by flicking his finger.

examples.ko: 친구는 제 이야기에 고개를 까닥거리면서 들었어요.
examples.en: My friend listened to my story, nodding slightly now and then.

explain: 한 번이 아니라 가볍게 여러 번 반복하는 느낌이에요. 한 번만 숙이는 동작은 '까닥'이라고 부사로 말해요. 리듬을 탈 때나 대답 대신 고개를 움직일 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The child was sleepy and bobbed his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까닥거리다'와 비슷하지만 한두 번 움직일 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 까닥거리다 but more natural for one or two movements.

phrases.en: I bob my head along to the music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 동작이 반복된다는 느낌을 부사로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb conveys the same small motion repeated.

phrases.en: He listened to my story with little nods.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'를 붙이면 다른 동작과 동시에 일어난다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -며 shows the nodding happens during another action.

explain_en: It gives the feeling of repeating a light movement several times. A single dip is expressed with the adverb '까닥'. You can use it for moving to a rhythm or for nodding in place of an answer.

en: to jump; to leap; to hop

examples.en: The puppy is so happy that it bounces around.
The kids play in the snow, leaping about.
A rabbit hopped across the meadow.
I was so excited that I bounded around and fell.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 껑충거려요? 무슨 좋은 일 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you bouncing like that? Did something good happen?

examples.ko: 그 사람은 다리가 길어서 껑충거리며 걸어요.
examples.en: He has long legs and walks with long bouncing strides.

explain: '껑충 뛰다'가 한 번 뛰는 것이라면, '껑충거리다'는 긴 다리로 계속 뛰어오르거나 큰 걸음으로 걷는 모습이에요. 작고 가벼운 동물에는 '깡충거리다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The child is so happy that he hops around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 뛰어다니는 모습을 부사 '껑충껑충'으로 더 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 껑충껑충 makes the repeated leaping more vivid.

phrases.en: The deer leapt and crossed the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 크게 뛰어오르는 것이라 '껑충거리다'와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a single big jump, unlike the repeated 껑충거리다.

phrases.en: The calf is bounding around in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '껑충거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 껑충거리다.

explain_en: '껑충 뛰다' is a single leap, while '껑충거리다' means leaping repeatedly or walking with long bouncing strides. For small, light animals, '깡충거리다' is also used.

examples.en: My father hammered away in the yard and made a chair.

examples.ko: 옆집에서 아침부터 뚝딱거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The neighbors were banging away from morning, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 하루 종일 뚝딱거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: There's a banging sound from the construction site all day.

examples.ko: 남편이 주말마다 뚝딱거리면 선반이 하나씩 생겨요.
examples.en: Every weekend my husband tinkers away and a new shelf appears.
My grandfather has been hammering and tinkering all day.

examples.ko: 작은 책꽂이는 한 시간쯤 뚝딱거렸더니 완성됐어요.
examples.en: After about an hour of hammering away, the small bookshelf was done.

explain: 망치질하거나 뭔가를 만들 때 나는 두드리는 소리와 그렇게 만드는 모습이에요. '뚝딱'만 쓰면 '뚝딱 만들다'처럼 금방 해치운다는 느낌이 되지만, '-거리다'는 소리가 이어지는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I've been hearing hammering sounds since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드리는 소리가 이어질 때 '-는 소리'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as '-는 소리' when the hammering keeps going.

phrases.en: My younger brother hammered away and made a bookshelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드리면서 무언가를 만드는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes making something while hammering.

phrases.en: They hammer all day long at the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속되는 일을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for something ongoing.

explain_en: It describes the pounding sounds of hammering or building something and the act of tinkering. '뚝딱' alone, as in '뚝딱 만들다', gives a sense of doing it quickly, while '-거리다' emphasizes the continuing sound.

examples.en: The market is swarming with people.
Tadpoles were swarming in the pond.
Bugs are swarming on the rotten fruit.
The beach is crawling with tourists on the weekend.
I was shocked because rats were swarming in the storeroom.
I want to avoid places teeming with people.

explain: 작은 것이나 사람이 좁은 곳에 많이 모여 움직일 때 써요. '북적거리다'가 활기찬 느낌이라면 '우글거리다'는 조금 답답하거나 지저분하다는 느낌이 있어요. 벌레, 쥐, 올챙이 같은 것에도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Rats are swarming in the drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우글대다'는 '우글거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '우글대다' means almost the same as '우글거리다'.

phrases.en: I saw bugs swarming on the rotten fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰고, 조금 불쾌한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, with a slightly unpleasant feeling.

phrases.en: People are swarming in front of the amusement park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 많이 모여 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a crowd moving around right now.

explain_en: It is used when many small things or people move around together in a tight space. While '북적거리다' feels lively, '우글거리다' can feel stuffy or unpleasant. It is often used for bugs, rats and tadpoles.

examples.en: The child is chewing slowly with food in the mouth.
Grandmother eats her rice slowly, chewing it over.

examples.ko: 그는 대답을 못 하고 우물거리기만 했어요.
examples.en: He couldn't answer and only mumbled.
Don't mumble; try speaking up.
I mumbled in the interview and couldn't finish what I wanted to say.
He mumbled something, but I couldn't make out a word.

explain: 입 안에서 음식을 씹는 모양과 말을 분명하지 않게 하는 모양, 두 가지로 써요. 말하는 쪽은 '웅얼거리다'나 '얼버무리다'와 비슷한데, '얼버무리다'는 일부러 분명하게 말하지 않는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Please don't mumble, and speak up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 분명하게 하라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone to speak clearly.

phrases.en: Grandfather walks along chewing on a candy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씹으면서 다른 동작을 함께 할 때 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This connective form links chewing with another action.

phrases.en: He mumbled something under his breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 입 밖으로 분명하게 나오지 않을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This collocation is for words that don't come out clearly.

explain_en: It is used both for chewing slowly in the mouth and for speaking unclearly. For speech it is close to '웅얼거리다' and '얼버무리다', and '얼버무리다' has a feel of deliberately not being clear.

en: to suffer; to bear the brunt

examples.ko: 사장이 시키는 대로 하느라 직원들만 죽어나요.
examples.en: Only the employees suffer, doing whatever the boss orders.

examples.ko: 일은 다 나한테 맡겨서 나만 죽어나는 거예요.
examples.en: They leave all the work to me, so I'm the only one who suffers.
They say the accounting team has a terrible time at year-end.
Every time the boss changed, only the staff below suffered.
You'll have a miserable time in this heat without air conditioning.
When adults fight, it's always the kids who suffer.

explain: 남의 일이나 상황 때문에 억울하게 고생할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '나만 죽어나다', '아랫사람만 죽어난다'처럼 '~만'과 함께 많이 써요. 일상에서는 불평하는 말투로 많이 들려요.

phrases.en: My teammates don't help, so I'm the only one suffering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기만 고생한다고 불평할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to complain that you alone are suffering.

phrases.en: When superiors make mistakes, only the subordinates suffer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘없는 사람이 대신 고생하는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when less powerful people suffer in someone else's place.

phrases.en: In the end, it's the employees who suffer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 고생하는지 강조하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress who ends up suffering.
phrases.en_equiv: the ones who suffer in the end are ~

explain_en: It is used when someone has a hard time unfairly because of other people or circumstances. It often pairs with '~만', as in '나만 죽어나다' or '아랫사람만 죽어난다'. In daily life it usually comes out as a complaint.

examples.en: The person upstairs thumps around every night, and it's hard on me.
The little kid came down the stairs thumping.
My heart is thumping, so I can't fall asleep.
Please don't thump so loudly in the hallway.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 쿵쿵거리며 방을 나갔어요.
examples.en: He was angry and stomped out of the room.
I walked with heavy thuds, carrying a heavy load.

explain: 무겁고 둔한 소리가 계속 나는 것을 말해요. 발소리, 문 소리, 심장 뛰는 소리에 두루 써요. '쿵쿵대다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 화가 나서 일부러 발소리를 크게 내며 걸을 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The kids are running around the house, thumping.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쿵쿵거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 입말 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '쿵쿵거리다', with a slightly more spoken feel.

phrases.en: I woke up because of the thumping sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 소음을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to describe a noise.

phrases.en: My angry dad walked off, stomping heavily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발소리를 크게 내며 걸을 때 써요. 화난 모습에도 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for walking with loud footsteps; fits an angry scene too.

explain_en: It describes a heavy, dull sound that keeps repeating. It works for footsteps, doors and a heartbeat. It is nearly the same as '쿵쿵대다'. It is also common when someone walks off angrily, stamping loudly.

examples.en: The kids sitting behind me are giggling.
The kids whisper and giggle under the blanket.
We giggled behind the teacher's back and got caught.
I turned at the sound of giggling and saw it was my friends.
My older sister, looking at her texts, is giggling to herself.

examples.ko: 장난이 재미있는지 동생이 키득키득 웃음을 참지 못해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling seems to find the prank funny and can't stop giggling.

explain: 웃음이 새어 나오는 작은 웃음소리를 계속 낼 때 써요. 한 번 짧게 웃으면 '킥'이라고 하고, '키득키득'은 여러 번 이어져요. 크게 웃는 '하하'나 '깔깔'과는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is giggling while reading a comic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키득키득'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with 키득키득.

phrases.en: Kids are giggling in the back of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사에 '-거리다'를 붙여 웃음이 이어진다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -거리다 to the adverb shows the giggling continues.

phrases.en: My friend giggled at those words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키득키득'보다 짧고 빠른 웃음소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, quicker laugh than 키득키득.

explain_en: It describes small laughs that leak out one after another. A single short laugh is '킥', while '키득키득' keeps going. It feels different from big laughs like '하하' or '깔깔'.
